draft.title: The price mechanism
card: Resources such as land, workers and materials are scarce. They cannot make everything people want, so they must be steered to where they are most wanted.
The price mechanism does this steering through prices. A price is a signal that tells buyers and sellers what to do.
a signal that a product is in high demand or short supply. Businesses may make more of it, and buyers may use less of it.
a signal that a product is less wanted or plentiful. Businesses may make less of it, and buyers may use more of it.
draft.remember: Prices are signals. They steer scarce resources to where they are most wanted.

a.q: What is the main job of the price mechanism?
opts: To steer scarce resources to where they are most wanted
To make sure every product costs the same amount
To stop businesses from making a profit on products
To decide which products the government will make
a.why: Changing prices signal to buyers and businesses what to do, which moves scarce resources to where they are most wanted. It does not make prices equal, because prices rise and fall with what people want.
a.clue: Think about what a price signal tells businesses and buyers.

b.q: A heatwave hits Mildura and the price of bottled water at the local shop rises. What signal does the higher price send to businesses?
opts: Water is in high demand, so selling more is worthwhile
Water is plentiful, so sellers should make less of it
Water is not wanted, so buyers will stop buying it
Water is cheap to make, so the shop should close
b.why: A rising price signals that a product is in high demand or short supply. Businesses may then make or sell more of it. The option about plentiful water has the signal reversed, because plentiful goods tend to fall in price.
b.clue: A rising price is a signal about how much people want a product.

a.best: To steer scarce resources to where they are most wanted

b.best: Water is in high demand, so selling more is worthwhile
